title: What does ConfidentialMPTSend do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of ConfidentialMPTSend and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, ConfidentialMPTSend transfers eligible MPTs while concealing the transfer amount through the documented cryptographic scheme. [1]

The transfer updates confidential balance commitments and requires proofs rather than a plain public amount alone. Confidentiality does not establish legal anonymity or remove issuer controls. Confirm the issuance supports the feature and the receiving state is usable. Wallet support, proof generation and network enablement are separate prerequisites for a working transfer. [1]

The ConfidentialMPTSend reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using ConfidentialMPTSend, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
